description: split() gives a set of strings: = and ≠ compare two of them, ⊆ and ⊈ test one in another, ∖ takes their difference, and ∈ and ∉ test a string in one. The alternative bad fails, since its pieces differ (engine §10).
grammar:
%rule text good | bad
%rule good $a(W) $b(W) $c(W)
%conditions split(phonemes($a), ".") = split(phonemes($b), "."), split(phonemes($a), ".") ≠ split(phonemes($c), "."), split(phonemes($a), ".") ⊆ split(phonemes($c), "."), split(phonemes($c), ".") ⊈ split(phonemes($a), "."), split(phonemes($c), ".") ∖ split(phonemes($a), ".") ≠ ∅, split(phonemes($b), ".") ∖ split(phonemes($a), ".") = ∅, "do" ∈ split(phonemes($c), "."), "do" ∉ split(phonemes($a), ".")
%rule bad $d(W) $e(W) $f(W)
%conditions split(phonemes($d), ".") = split(phonemes($f), ".")
